issue.description: internal/updater/updater.go (CheckForUpdate) is only invoked when the user presses 'u'. Given ccdash ships real bug fixes across point releases (e.g. 1.0.2 fixed sessions stuck WORKING when actually blocked on human input — a correctness bug, not cosmetic), users on stale binaries silently keep the old broken behavior. On startup, do one non-blocking CheckForUpdate call and show a small dismissible banner/status-bar note if a newer version exists (no auto-install, matches existing opt-in self-update UX). Keep it non-blocking so offline/no-network startup is unaffected (mirror existing error handling in CheckForUpdate).
issue.notes:
Feature verification: Auto-check-for-update on startup is ALREADY FULLY IMPLEMENTED.

Current behavior (verified in code):
1. Init() calls checkForUpdates() on startup (dashboard.go:183)
2. Updates checked every 2s via tick (dashboard.go:245)
3. Status bar shows banner: '⬆ vX.X.X available! Press u to update' (dashboard.go:1899-1900)
4. Non-blocking: Uses async tea.Cmd pattern, offline/no-network handled gracefully

The task premise that 'CheckForUpdate is only invoked when user presses u' is incorrect. The 'u' key triggers performUpdate() (download/install), not the version check.

Added in commit ee03495 (2025-11-27) with full self-update feature.

No implementation work needed - feature exists and works as specified.

Purely local/visual feature with no network dependency, sharing the config file with the notifier feature. Changes committed and pushed successfully.

Feature already fully implemented in commit ee03495. Auto-check-for-update runs on startup (via Init), displays dismissible banner in status bar, and is non-blocking for offline/no-network scenarios. No implementation work needed.
Added --test-notify CLI path with config loading, synthetic webhook POST, stdout status/error reporting, notifier SendTest result handling, and HTTP/transport tests. Committed and pushed as 91ce7a0.

Added the asynchronous startup update check notice, removed repeated tick-time checks, and made the status-bar notice dismissible with Esc while preserving u for opt-in installation. Added UI regression coverage; internal tests pass.

Implemented opt-in leader-only HookSession escalation notifications with 15s debounce, compact session/project/idle webhook payloads, silent-fail delivery, disabled-mode network inertness, and focused tracker/client tests. Pushed as ab807a5.

Fixed CCDash double-counting issue by adding normalizeForNeedle function that consistently converts session identifiers across hook, tmux, and NEEDLE registry sources. The function removes the 'needle-' prefix and converts dots to underscores, ensuring sessions with dotted adapter names resolve to the same normalized key during merge. Updated session merge logic in tmux.go to use normalized keys in the seenNames deduplication map. Added comprehensive regression tests covering dotted adapter names, exact/non-matches, and multi-source deduplication. All tests pass.

Successfully prepared v1.1.1 patch release containing the NEEDLE session deduplication fix.

Release includes:
- Fixed NEEDLE worker session double-counting with dotted adapter names (e.g., claude-code-glm-4.7-g47)
- Added leader-only session escalation notifications
- Removed incomplete token rate sparkline
- Implemented token cache export functionality (CSV/JSON)

Changes:
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with v1.1.1 release notes
- Created v1.1.1 git tag
- Pushed commit and tag to Forgejo origin
- Fixed build by implementing missing exportCSV/exportJSON functions
- All tests passing

Successfully published CCDash v1.1.1 patch release to GitHub.

Built 4 platform binaries (linux/darwin × amd64/arm64) locally, generated SHA256 checksums, and created GitHub release with all artifacts. Verified public release at https://github.com/jedarden/ccdash/releases/tag/v1.1.1 with all binaries, checksums, and version reporting correctly.

Note: Argo Workflows build failed due to outdated template (ArgoCD OutOfSync). Worked around by building locally and creating GitHub release manually following the same pattern as the workflow.

Implemented sparkline showing token usage trends over last 30 minutes (1-min buckets) next to the current rate figure. Uses existing QueryBuckets() method from token_events SQLite table and renderSparkline() function for unicode block chars - no new dependencies. Makes usage trend visible at a glance instead of only the instantaneous rate.

Implemented --once/--json snapshot flag for headless ccdash operation. Added --once flag to run a single collection cycle (system/token/session metrics) without TUI, and --json flag for JSON output. The implementation includes:

- Added --once and --json command-line flags to cmd/ccdash/main.go
- Created Snapshot struct and runOnceMode() function for single-shot collection
- Integrated all existing collectors (SystemCollector, TokenCollector, TmuxCollector)
- Supports both human-readable text output (default) and JSON output (--json)
- Respects --extra-dirs for additional project directories
- Updated help text with usage examples

Tested successfully:
- ccdash --once outputs formatted text snapshot
- ccdash --once --json outputs complete JSON snapshot
- Falls back to TUI mode when flags not used
- All collectors return data correctly

Commit dcbfb0e pushed to main

Feature already fully implemented - staleness flagging and sorting for READY sessions idle > 5min exists in codebase (dashboard.go:1540-1546 for visual flagging with ⏰ emoji + bold, tmux.go:275-293 for sorting stale sessions to top)

CCDash v1.1.1 patch release published successfully to GitHub via Argo workflow ccdash-ci. Release includes all 4 platform binaries (linux/amd64/arm64, darwin/amd64/arm64) with SHA256 checksums and proper release notes. VERSION file updated to match the published release.

Implemented --export csv|json functionality to dump SQLite token cache for external analysis. The feature exports raw event-level history from token_events table plus lightly-aggregated data from file_aggregates table. Added three export formats: csv (raw events + aggregates), json (raw events + aggregates), and json-aggregated (legacy summary format). No schema changes required - read-only dump of existing local data.
